title: Sales Enablement Playbook — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pricing, Pitch Decks, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's core go-to-market assets for sales and solutions teams: unified positioning and messaging, concise competitive briefs, recommended pitch deck structure, pricing guidance by motion, reproducible case study templates, and a customer-facing Security & Compliance FAQ for prospects. Use this playbook to accelerate discovery calls, standardize proposals, and reduce time-to-first-value in trial and enterprise motions.

Audience: Solutions Engineers, Account Executives, Sales Engineers, Customer Success, Field Marketing, and Partner reps.

Owner & maintenance
- Primary owner: Go-to-market content (Aisha Patel)
- Secondary owners: Product Marketing (Marco Ruiz), Security & Compliance (Tomasz Lewandowski)
- Review cadence: Quarterly or when major product/pricing/security changes occur

1) Positioning & messaging (elevator + extended)
- Elevator pitch (30s): "Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLMs predictable and economical in production — whether hosted, dedicated, or private. We reduce latency and per-token cost while providing enterprise controls for security and compliance."
- 2–3 key value props (customer-facing bullets):
  - Performance & predictability: SLA-backed latency tiers and dedicated capacity options reduce tail latency and repeated tuning.
  - Cost controls: Batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations cut per-token cost without compromising quality.
  - Deployment flexibility: Single API and tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments for consistent developer experience.
  - Enterprise readiness: Audit logs, KMS integrations, and private control-plane options for regulated customers.
- Proof points and metrics to cite:
  - Typical latency: p95 text-gen < 150ms for short-turn prompts on dedicated capacity (customer workload dependent).
  - Cost savings: 20–60% unit-cost reduction using recommended batching and cache profiles vs. naively-hosted endpoints (internal benchmark).
  - Time-to-first-value: self-serve API + quickstart templates allow integration in <1 day for PoC.

2) Competitive brief (short format for battlecards)
- Competitors to highlight: General cloud AI platforms (managed endpoints), LLM API providers, self-hosted inference runtimes.
- Differentiators (talking points):
  - Unified runtime + ops: single control plane across hosted/dedicated/private (vs. cloud-managed services that fragment tooling).
  - Cost-aware controls: explicit batching/caching/quantization guidance and tooling (vs. providers with limited unit-economics transparency).
  - Enterprise-first fallbacks: automatic model fallbacks and region-aware routing for reliability (vs. DIY infra).

Quick battlecard template (use in call):
- Customer need: e.g., low-latency search rerank at scale with cost budget
- Redwood advantage: predictable latency via Dedicated + autoscaling policies, KV cache to reduce recompute, cost guidance that maps to tokens saved
- Objection + response: "We can self-host for cheaper." → "Self-hosting often shifts engineering cost; Redwood reduces ops burden with pre-tuned kernels, autoscaling, and observability that directly lowers long-term TCO."

3) Pitch deck skeleton (recommended slide order)
- Title & intro: 1 slide (value prop + logo + date)
- Customer pain & context: 1–2 slides (e.g., latency, cost, reliability)
- Redwood solution overview: 1 slide (hosted / dedicated / private)
- How it works: 2 slides (serving runtime, routing, caching & batching)
- Performance & cost benchmarks: 1–2 slides (representative numbers and methodology)
- Security & compliance: 1 slide (KMS, audit logs, private control plane)
- Integrations & SDKs: 1 slide (REST/SDKs, streaming, function-calling)
- Pricing & commercial fit: 1 slide (high level; link to pricing guidance)
- Case study / reference: 1 slide (customer impact metrics)
- Next steps & ask: 1 slide (trial, POC scope, stakeholders)

Presentation tips: lead with the customer's highest-cost pain (latency or ops), call out the concrete SLOs we can support, and always close with a precise next step (e.g., 2-week PoC with a dedicated capacity evaluation).

4) Pricing guidance (motion-specific recommendations)
- Self-serve / SMB: promote hosted API; emphasize per-token pricing and free credits for trial. Recommend pilot limits: 100k tokens/day initial threshold.
- Mid-market / growth: propose Dedicated baseline with monthly commit + 30% buffer for traffic spikes. Include 90-day review to tune autoscale policies.
- Enterprise / regulated: offer Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) + support package. Commercials: platform fee + reserved capacity contract (annual commit).
- Discounting guardrails:
  - SMB: max 15% discount off list for >$10k ARR logo motion
  - Dedicated: tiered discounts starting at 12-month commit; escalate approvals for >25% discount
- Commercial play: include a two-step quote: (1) baseline reserved capacity (GPU-hours or vCPU/GPU capacity units), (2) optional add-ons: extended retention, premium SLAs, on-prem packaging.

5) Case study template (repeatable for sales collateral)
- One-line summary: customer, solution, and headline metric (e.g., "Acme Search reduced re-rank latency 3x and cut per-query cost 40% using Redwood Dedicated").
- Challenge: 2–3 bullets describing initial pain, baseline metrics.
- Solution: config used (model family, Dedicated/Dedicated+KV cache, batching profile, autoscale policy).
- Results (quantified): list of metrics pre/post (latency p95, tokens per query, cost per 1k queries, adoption/usage growth).
- Timeline & team: pilot length, teams involved, owners.
- Quote & contact: customer quote and internal reference.

6) Security & Compliance FAQ for prospects (customer-facing - keep concise)
- Q: Where is customer data stored?
  A: By default in our hosted control plane region selected by the customer; customers may choose Dedicated in a customer-owned VPC or Private on-prem deployment for full data residency requirements.
- Q: Do you support KMS / HSM?
  A: Yes. We integrate with major KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and support HSM-backed key management for Private deployments.
- Q: How is audit logging handled?
  A: All control-plane actions and inference requests can be routed to an audit log stream with configurable retention; logs include request metadata (non-sensitive) and are available for 90 days by default with extended retention as an add-on.
- Q: Can you run in an air-gapped environment?
  A: Yes — our Private on-prem package supports air-gapped deployments; see onprem-packaging guide for installation and hardening steps.
- Q: What certifications/compliance do you have?
  A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II for hosted and Dedicated control plane operations and is pursuing ISO 27001. For regulated customers we provide artifact packages and a compliance onboarding checklist.

7) Reusable sales artifacts (where to find)
- Pitch decks: /confluence/sales-enablement/pitch-decks (canonical decks by motion)
- Demos & quickstarts: eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates (PoC repos and sample apps)
- Technical deep-dives: eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture and benchmarking-and-perf-suite
- Security collateral: security-and-compliance/audit-logging and data-residency-and-retention

8) Playbook flows (recommended sequences)
- Self-serve discovery (SMB): trial sign-up → guided quickstart → usage checkpoint email at day 3 → champion handoff to solutions for expansion.
- PoC to Dedicated (mid-market): discovery → scoping doc + pilot plan (2 wks) → pilot on Dedicated with monitoring dashboard → results review and commit proposal.
- Enterprise procurement (regulated): security questionnaire → architecture review with eng-private-deployments → compliance artifact package → contract and on-prem/private deployment planning.

9) Templates & checklists (copy these into deals)
- Discovery checklist: integration points (API, SDK), expected QPS, latency SLO, data residency, security controls, stakeholders.
- Pilot success criteria: p95 latency target, cost per 1k requests target, correctness QA pass rate on sample prompts, retention/usage baseline.

10) Acceptance & next steps for GTM teams
- Use this playbook as the canonical starting point for new deals. Pull case-study and benchmark numbers from eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite and reference security artifacts when customers request them.
- Request updates or file issues with go-to-market-content@redwood.ai.

Appendix: Example customer case (Acme Search) — concise
- Challenge: high re-rank latency (p95 420ms) and high per-query cost at scale.
- Redwood solution: Dedicated pool (4x A100 equiv), KV prefix caching, model quantization profile q4_0, autoscale policy with 2x burst.
- Outcome: p95 improved to 120ms, per-query cost down 42%, adoption increased 3x in 8 weeks.
